intent: Evaluate exact GBJ2510-F through the actual Gmsh/Elmer FEM path and four-diode/case thermal network. Bind the result to the mandatory Rust harness while retaining native-source authority and explicit INDETERMINATE status for unknown internal thermal paths, installed airflow, and unresolved AC2 sharing.
reviewers: adversarial-claude (not run; host approval rejected egress)

learnings.title: FEM power balance needs independently checked domains and ports
learnings.note: The retained GBJ replay follows independent domain, port, per-contact, and global balance checks.

learnings.title: External FEM is a validity proxy, not a hardware certificate
learnings.note: The harness keeps hardware applicability and installed cooling indeterminate after numerical replay.

learnings.title: Model certificates need semantic binding in addition to hashes
learnings.note: Native identity, UUIDs, source bytes, and rejecting controls are retained across the GBJ path.

learnings.title: Measurement conventions and source identities must be explicit
learnings.note: Cooling catalog points, FEM reservoirs, and point-estimate VF are labeled as conditional assumptions.

residual_risks: Unknown package internals and mutual die paths remain indeterminate.
Installed airflow, shutdown timing, and full-board current distribution remain unverified.
AC2 uses an explicit full-terminal RMS sensitivity because no determined copper cut exists; this is not a resolved current-sharing claim.
The live round/back Gmsh test is ignored in ordinary test runs, although a separately executed live Gmsh/Elmer pass and bound raw evidence were reviewed.
testing_gaps: Consider a pinned portable Gmsh CI path for the ignored round/back geometry test; this is follow-up tooling and does not invalidate the bound live study.
